attempt.narrative: Fake Out denied Bronzong turn 1 but Dusclops set Trick Room anyway, which is the room working as designed. Under the room Dusclops burned Urshifu, which cost me my best breaker for the rest of the fight, and Bronzong's Body Press plus Night Shade drove it to 15. Three always-crit Wicked Blows removed Dusclops. Trick Room ran its full five turns. Knock Off one-shot Chimecho from full HP, Porygon2 arrived with Download and traded Zapdos for itself, and Mega Gengar - immune to High Jump Kick, immune to Tri Attack, and carrying a Ghost attack that is 2x into four of the six - closed the room by one-shotting Mega Medicham on its transformation turn.

protect_ledger_build16.payoff: Blocked Incineroar's Flare Blitz, 2x into Steel/Psychic. Magnitude is proven, not estimated: the same Flare Blitz landed on turn 3 and took Bronzong from 243 to 1. The guard bought the setter a full extra turn under its own Trick Room.

Nothing was aimed at Chimecho. My Knock Off went to the 1 HP Bronzong and my other slot spent the turn switching a burned 15 HP Urshifu out for Zapdos. The guard blocked zero damage and produced zero progress.
protect_ledger_build16.forecast_defence: Stronger than the prior receipt allowed for, and it should be recorded. Incineroar's Knock Off was already a revealed move and it is a genuine ONE-SHOT on this Chimecho - proven on turn 5, where it KOed Chimecho from a full 283 HP in a single hit. So a freshly entered Chimecho was guarding against a revealed, lethal, adjacent attack under a mixed forecast, which is exactly what the no-omniscience design asks it to price. It is empty in outcome, not obviously wrong in expectation. Counted as empty for the before/after number all the same.

comparison_to_prior_receipt.prior_ledger_scope: receipt.json, same party and same seed on build-6, recorded four opponent Protects: Bronzong T2 (excellent), Chimecho T4 (EMPTY), Cofagrigus T6 (EMPTY), Cofagrigus T9 (excellent).
comparison_to_prior_receipt.verdict: Half fixed. Cofagrigus's empty guard is gone and was replaced by a genuinely excellent one - on the same turn number, the same battler now guards a board where both of my actions were actually aimed at it, and it blocked a 2x Knock Off and a spread Heat Wave together. Chimecho's turn-4 empty guard recurred unchanged: same turn, same first-turn-out board, same zero payoff. This is the one place in my whole block where a prior empty guard was reproduced, and it is the concrete residual finding of this pass.
comparison_to_prior_receipt.chimecho_residual_analysis: Worth being precise about, because it may not be a scoring bug at all. The board on turn 4 was: Chimecho fresh at 283/283 with Rocky Helmet, its partner Bronzong on 1 HP and certain to die, Trick Room active, and opposite it an Incineroar whose Knock Off had already been revealed and is a proven one-shot on Chimecho. Guarding a lethal revealed threat on a freshly entered body is defensible expected value under a mixed forecast; what made it empty is that I spent Knock Off finishing the 1 HP partner instead. If this is to be tuned, the lever is probably the forecast's weighting of an opponent that has an obvious higher-value target elsewhere on the board (a 1 HP ally), not the guard scoring itself. Recorded as a finding for the AI side rather than as an illegal choice.

level_rule_statement: APPLIED, and this is the one room in my block where the outcome flips the prior receipt's decision, so I am stating it explicitly. The prior receipt decided KEEP on the strength of a 6-2 win. This rerun, on the same party and the same seed, won 6-1 in 8 turns instead of 10 - a first-attempt win with a single player faint. That is the brief's rule 5 trigger ('won first try with 0-1 player faints') and AGENTS.md's Gym standard reinforces it: 'Every Gym trainer should be an exceptional difficulty benchmark' and 'A comfortable win deserves scrutiny', against a stated aim of roughly three player faints. Two of my six were never touched at all. I have applied the minimum permitted lever: +1 on ONE member, the maximum of the plus-or-minus-1 allowed this pass. Chimecho is the choice because the brief says the weakest one or two members and never the ace or Mega first: all five non-Mega members share the lowest offset (+1), and among them Chimecho is plainly the weakest build - no Eviolite, 4 Def EVs, and it was the only member one-shot from full HP. Mega Medicham (+2) was excluded as the ace. Honest caveats, both of which the main agent should weigh: (a) I cannot retest this, because a level change needs a rebuild and this brief forbids me from running make, so the +1 is recorded for materialization and native retest by the main agent; (b) AGENTS.md says fix AI defects before compensating with levels, and this room still has one - Chimecho's empty turn-4 guard, P16-V1. I judged the win comfortable independently of that defect, because a Dazzling Gleam on turn 4 instead of the guard would not have produced a second faint; but if the AI side would rather fix P16-V1 first and re-measure, reverting this single line is the correct call and I would not argue with it.
could_this_be_cooler: The concept is excellent and no composition change is recommended - the dossier's claim that every non-setter is chosen for what it does to the player holds up, and Dusclops's Will-O-Wisp removing my Urshifu from the fight with one status move is the memory the room actually leaves. The real problem is not coolness, it is ordering: Mega Medicham, the advertised payoff, has now arrived AFTER Trick Room expired in both recorded runs, so Pure Power under reversed order - the whole point of the room - has never once happened. It came in fifth and sixth respectively. That is a switch-order and deployment question for the AI side rather than a design change, and fixing it would do far more for this room than any level would. Second, smaller note: Cofagrigus's Mummy also went untested for the second time, because the dossier publishes the counterplay ('do not make contact') clearly enough that a prepared player simply never touches it.
